transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I came in because I just can't seem to get anything in order anymore. 

It's... my kitchen table is just covered. My husband's appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center... half-finished lists. I just... I sit there. I don't know which thing to do first, and then... well, the whole day is just gone.
About how long have you been noticing this trouble with getting things organized?

I suppose it's been this much trouble for... maybe a year and three months. Right around the time when... well, when my husband started needing regular help. Just with his appointments and daily arrangements.
Do you find it difficult or painful to throw any of these papers away?
No... I wouldn't say that. Um. It's not painful. I don't really care about keeping them. I just... I never seem to get around to actually throwing them out.
Over the past few months, have you been feeling down, depressed, or sad most days?
No... I don't think so. Just tired, mostly.
Besides the trouble with organizing, have you noticed any problems with your memory, such as forgetting recent events or conversations?
No, not really. I mean... I might forget little things sometimes, but... nothing unusual. Just the normal amount, I suppose.
Growing up or earlier in your life, did you ever struggle with staying organized, paying attention, or finishing tasks?

I suppose so. Um... even when I was a little girl, really. My teachers used to write that I was... bright, but careless. I'd forget my books, or my homework. They always had to remind me to finish my seatwork... before I could go outside. Just... things like that.
Do you often find yourself feeling restless, fidgeting, or having trouble sitting still?

Well... yes, I suppose so. I try to sit still, especially if I'm somewhere I'm supposed to be polite, like a meeting or... something like that. But I just... I end up rubbing my hands together, or tapping my foot. Or clicking a pen. I shift around a lot in my chair. Sometimes I think I do it so much that... well, people look over at me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with prominent symptoms of inattention (severe disorganization, difficulty initiating and prioritizing tasks, leaving tasks unfinished) and hyperactivity/restlessness (fidgeting with hands, foot tapping, shifting constantly in her seat). A childhood history of inattention and disorganization ('bright but careless', forgetting books/homework, needing reminders to finish seatwork) establishes the chronic, neurodevelopmental nature of the condition, which has decompensated into marked functional impairment under increased caregiver responsibilities. Hoarding disorder and depressive or neurocognitive disorders were evaluated and ruled out.
